module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Recurrence $a(n) = (a(n-1) + a(n-2)) \pmod n$

$a(0) = a(1) = 1$; $a(n) = (a(n-1) + a(n-2)) \pmod n$.

*References:*
- [A096535](https://oeis.org/A096535)-/

@[expose] public section

namespace OeisA96535

/-- Recurrence $a(n) = (a(n-1) + a(n-2)) \pmod n$. -/
def a : ℕ → ℕ
  | 0 => 1
  | 1 => 1
  | n + 2 => (a (n + 1) + a n) % (n + 2)

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 0. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_0 : a 0 = 1 := by rfl

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 1. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_1 : a 1 = 1 := by rfl

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 2. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : a 2 = 0 := by rfl

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 3. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_3 : a 3 = 1 := by rfl

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 4. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_4 : a 4 = 1 := by rfl

/--
All numbers appear infinitely often, i.e., for every number $k \ge 0$ and every frequency $f > 0$
there is an index $i$ such that $a(i) = k$ is the $f$-th occurrence of $k$ in the sequence.
- _Klaus Brockhaus_, Aug 29 2006
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture (k : ℕ) (N : ℕ) : ∃ i : ℕ, i > N ∧ a i = k := by
  sorry

end OeisA96535

reformulations.difference: The source asserts that every natural number k has an f-th occurrence for every positive f. Lean instead asserts that, for every index bound N, some i > N satisfies a i = k.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For each k, the occurrence indices form a subset of ℕ. Being unbounded is equivalent to being infinite, which supplies an f-th occurrence for every positive f. Conversely, choosing the (N+2)-nd occurrence gives an index i with N+2 ≤ i+1, hence i > N. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, both the infinitude equivalence and the exact equivalence with ∀ f > 0, ∃ i, a i = k ∧ Nat.count (fun j => a j = k) (i+1) = f were proved without using the conjecture or sorry.

sources_consulted: OEIS A096535, including all three conjectures and subsequent comments, read through the official data mirror: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A096/A096535.seq
